Annual.
Interval: VIPoma resected 11/2024 (G1, clear margins, 0/8 nodes); VIP normal in Feb. Bowels normal since surgery.
Still gets headaches a few times a week, worse on long days. Fatigue at the end of the day. No chest pain or palpitations.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, KCl 40 BID, pantoprazole 40. NKDA.
Exam: BP as recorded, R 150/96 L 148/94. Well. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, healed port scars, no masses. Breasts normal. Skin sun damage, nothing suspicious. Trace edema.

2. Pancreatic NET (VIPoma), resected - surveillance CT Nov per surg onc.
3. PUD - stable.
4. Preventive: mammogram ordered, Pap 2024 normal, colonoscopy 2023 normal. Flu/COVID in fall.
Video BP check in June.

medications.sig: Dissolve 1 tablet on the tongue every 8 hours as needed for nausea

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of visit: 09/15/2025

CC: vomiting.
HPI: 47-year-old woman with primary hyperaldosteronism, a resected pancreatic VIPoma and a history of peptic ulcer disease, with two days of severe nausea and vomiting many times a day. She cannot keep down food or fluids. For the past few weeks she has also had intermittent epigastric pain. No diarrhea, no blood in the vomit, no fever.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, potassium chloride 40 mEq BID, pantoprazole 40.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 100/60, HR 110. Dry mucous membranes, looks dehydrated. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding, no distension.

Labs: Na 140, K 2.9, Cl 90, HCO3 32, BUN 28, Cr 1.0. Urine chloride 10 mEq/L. Lipase normal. CBC and magnesium normal.

ED course: 2 L normal saline with 20 mEq KCl per liter, ondansetron 4 mg IV, pantoprazole 40 mg IV. Nausea settled; tolerated crackers and fluids; oral potassium chloride 40 mEq given. Repeat HR 88, BP 124/78.

Impression: hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis from vomiting, with hypovolemia and dehydration; hypokalemia, taking oral replacement and tolerating it.
Disposition: home. Ondansetron 4 mg ODT every 8 hours as needed. Continue home medications. PCP within 2-3 days and GI follow-up for the epigastric pain. Return for persistent vomiting, blood, black stool or worsening pain.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ED Mon night for 2 days of vomiting - fluids, potassium, home. Vomiting stopped Tuesday; used 2 ondansetron since. Eating soft foods and drinking well. Epigastric burning on and off for a few weeks before this, a bit better now. No black stools. No NSAIDs. Takes pantoprazole every morning.
O: BP as recorded, HR normal. Mucosa moist. Abd soft, minimal epigastric tenderness, no guarding.
ED labs reviewed: Cl 90, HCO3 32, K 2.9, urine Cl 10 - contraction/vomiting alkalosis.
A/P
1. Vomiting with hypochloremic alkalosis and dehydration - clinically resolved; BMP today to confirm.
2. Epigastric pain with PUD history - GI already asked to see her; EGD referral placed. Continue pantoprazole daily.
3. HTN/aldosteronism/hypokalemia - back on all meds, continue KCl 40 BID.
Call if vomiting returns.

documents.title: BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium back up, kidney numbers and bicarbonate back to your usual. Good. GI should be calling about the scope.

reports.text:
Specimen: gastric antrum and body, cold forceps biopsies.
Microscopic: gastric mucosa without significant histopathologic abnormality. No Helicobacter-like organisms on routine and immunohistochemical stains. No intestinal metaplasia or dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Gastric biopsies, antrum and body: no significant abnormality; negative for H. pylori.

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOSCOPY CENTER - EGD REPORT
Procedure date: 10/14/2025
Indication: epigastric pain and recent vomiting; history of peptic ulcer disease.
NKDA. Monitored anesthesia care.
Findings: normal esophagus and GE junction. Stomach normal; biopsies of antrum and body for H. pylori. Duodenal bulb with scarring and mild deformity from prior ulcer disease; no active ulcer. Pylorus and bulb passed easily - no outlet obstruction. Second portion of duodenum normal.
Pathology: negative for H. pylori.
Impression: healed duodenal bulb ulcer scar; no active ulcer or obstruction.
Recommendation: continue pantoprazole 40 mg daily; avoid NSAIDs.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: surveillance, one year after distal pancreatectomy for well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor.
Comparison: 04/02/2024.
Findings: post-surgical changes of distal pancreatectomy with surgical clips at the resection margin. No soft tissue at the resection bed. The remaining pancreatic head and body enhance normally; duct not dilated. Spleen preserved, normal size, splenic vein patent. Liver without focal lesions. Adrenal glands unremarkable. Kidneys normal. No lymphadenopathy or ascites. Pelvic organs unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Expected post-pancreatectomy changes. No evidence of recurrent or metastatic disease.

medications.sig: Take 2 capsules (60 mg) by mouth every 4 hours through 04/15/2026

reports.text:
Indication: sudden severe headache with neck stiffness.
Technique: axial noncontrast CT of the head.
Findings: hyperdense acute blood fills the prepontine and interpeduncular cisterns around the brainstem and extends into the basal cisterns. Ventricles normal in size; no hydrocephalus. No intraparenchymal hematoma. No midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage around the brainstem and in the basal cisterns. No hydrocephalus.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of visit: 03/26/2026

CC: headache.
HPI: 48-year-old woman with primary hyperaldosteronism and a resected pancreatic VIPoma, who has had chronic headaches and recurrent low potassium. About an hour before arrival, while working in a garden bed, she had an abrupt, severe headache - the worst she has ever had - with a stiff neck and light hurting her eyes. No trauma. No loss of consciousness reported.
Meds: lisinopril, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, potassium chloride 40 mEq BID, pantoprazole 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father died of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm at 67.

Exam: BP 158/94, HR 102, T 37.2 C (99 F). Awake and alert but anxious. Nuchal rigidity. Pupils equal and reactive, cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation symmetric - no focal deficit. GCS 15.

Noncontrast head CT: acute subarachnoid blood around the brainstem and in the basal cisterns.

Impression: acute subarachnoid hemorrhage, presumed aneurysmal.
Plan: neurosurgery and neurocritical care consulted; blood pressure lowered with IV nicardipine; CT angiography; admit to neuro ICU.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Neurocritical Care
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/26/2026. Discharged 04/09/2026.

Principal diagnosis: aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured basilar tip aneurysm.
Other: primary hyperaldosteronism with resistant hypertension; chronic hypokalemia; resected pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (VIPoma); peptic ulcer disease.
Allergies: NKDA.

Presentation: sudden worst-ever headache while gardening, neck stiffness and photophobia; BP 158/94, HR 102; nuchal rigidity without focal deficit. Head CT showed subarachnoid blood around the brainstem and basal cisterns.

Course:
- CT angiography 03/26: 7 mm aneurysm at the basilar tip; no other aneurysm.
- Endovascular coil embolization the night of 03/26 via right femoral access, with complete occlusion of the aneurysm. No complications.
- Neuro ICU: nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours started on admission for a 21-day course. Blood pressure controlled with IV nicardipine, then her home lisinopril, amlodipine and hydrochlorothiazide. Daily neuro checks and transcranial ultrasound showed no vasospasm. No hydrocephalus. Potassium replaced as needed in addition to her home dose.
- Moved to the neuroscience floor on day 9; walking independently; headache improving on scheduled acetaminophen.

Discharge exam: alert, oriented, fluent; no focal deficit.

Discharge medications: nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours through 04/15/2026, then stop; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 10 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; potassium chloride 40 mEq twice daily; pantoprazole 40 mg daily.
Instructions: no driving or heavy lifting until cleared by neurosurgery; return for new severe headache, weakness, confusion or seizure.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; neurosurgery clinic in 4 weeks; follow-up angiography about 6 months after coiling.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call day after discharge. Pt home. Headache 3/10, using acetaminophen. Taking nimodipine every 4 hrs - set phone alarms, last dose 4/15. Has all home meds. No new weakness, confusion or vomiting. Groin site fine. Appt with Dr 4/16 confirmed. Return precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u. Ruptured basilar tip aneurysm 3/26 with SAH, coiled same night, 14 days inpatient, no vasospasm or hydrocephalus. Discharged 4/9. Driven in today.
S: Headache easing, 1-3/10, acetaminophen once a day. Tired, napping. Neck less stiff. Finished nimodipine yesterday. No weakness, numbness, speech or vision problems. Eating fine. Groin site healed.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, KCl 40 BID, pantoprazole 40. Nimodipine completed. NKDA.
O: BP as recorded. Alert, oriented, conversant. CN II-XII intact, strength 5/5 throughout, sensation and gait normal. Neck supple. Heart RRR. R groin no hematoma or bruit.
A/P
1. SAH from ruptured basilar aneurysm, s/p coiling - neurologically intact. Neurosurgery clinic 5/7; angiogram ~6 mo. No driving until neurosurgery clears.
2. Resistant HTN / primary hyperaldosteronism - BP 148/92, too high after an aneurysm bleed. Home log BID for 4 wks and bring it; we'll decide on the regimen at the next visit with neurosurgery input. BMP today.
3. Hypokalemia - continue 40 BID.
RTC 4 wks.

documents.title: Neurosurgery Clinic Note
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROSURGERY - CLINIC LETTER
Date of visit: 05/07/2026

Six weeks after endovascular coiling of a ruptured 7 mm basilar tip aneurysm. She is doing well: headaches are now mild and infrequent, energy improving, no new neurologic symptoms. Neurologic exam is normal. Access site healed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: cleared to drive and to return gradually to work, avoiding heavy straining for another month. Follow-up catheter angiography about 6 months after coiling; our office will schedule. Blood pressure control is important - goal below 130/80; management per her PCP.

Outside neurosurgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 7 wks after SAH/coiling. Neurosurgery 5/7: doing well, cleared to drive and ease back to work, BP goal <130/80. Headaches mild, a couple a week. Back to light jobs, her helpers doing the digging.
Home log 4 wks (BID): average ~150/92, few readings under 140.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, KCl 40 BID, pantoprazole 40. NKDA.
O: BP as recorded, repeat 150/94. Neuro nonfocal. RRR. Lungs clear. Trace edema.
4/16 BMP: K low as usual on 40 BID, creatinine normal.

A/P
1. Primary hyperaldosteronism with resistant HTN, after a ruptured aneurysm - not at goal on lisinopril/amlodipine/HCTZ. The drug that targets the cause is an aldosterone blocker. Starting spironolactone 25 mg daily and stopping HCTZ (it wastes potassium and adds little here). Discussed breast tenderness, menstrual changes, and that potassium can swing high with spironolactone plus lisinopril.
2. Hypokalemia - cutting KCl to 20 mEq twice daily (1 tab BID) now; BMP in 1 week, will adjust by phone.
3. SAH s/p coiling - angio ~6 mo per neurosurgery.
4. Pantoprazole continues.
Home BP log; send readings in 2-3 wks. RTC September.

documents.title: BMP on spironolactone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Paula - potassium 4.0, the most normal it has been in years, and kidney function is normal (creatinine 0.9). Stay on the current doses. Keep the BP log coming.

documents.title: BP log
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two weeks on the new pill. Mornings: 138/86, 136/84, 140/88, 134/84, 137/86, 132/82, 135/85. Evenings similar. Headaches less. A little breast soreness but tolerable.

documents.title: RE: BP log
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's the best stretch you've had since I've known you. Not quite at the 130/80 goal yet, and spironolactone can keep working for a few more weeks, so no change now. Let me know if the breast soreness gets bothersome. We'll go over it in September.
